answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance arises when each identity must post a bonded stake that peers can slash upon detecting coordinated fakes. Genuine agents produce velvet-smooth, continuous work near the reef of shared tasks, while attackers cluster abruptly. The attacker pays by locking capital for every duplicate on the horizon of possible identities; once the jury flags the pattern the bonds are lost, making large-scale identity farming economically painful rather than free.
